Events of February 1848 in France had brought about the abdication of the monarch and a republic based on universal male suffrage had been proclaimed. questions.answer: (d) Liberals — the 1848 revolution of the liberals refers to the national movements pioneered by the educated middle classes alongside the revolts of the poor, unemployed and starving peasants and workers in Europe.

or.text: Who was Giuseppe Garibaldi? What was his contribution in the freedom Movement of Italy?
or.answer:
Giuseppe Garibaldi is the most celebrated Italian freedom fighter. He came from a family engaged in coastal trade and was a sailor in the merchant navy.
His contribution: In 1833 he met Mazzini and joined the Young Italy movement and participated in a republican uprising in Piedmont in 1834. The uprising was suppressed. Garibaldi had to flee to South America, where he lived in exile till 1848. In 1854, he supported Victor Emmanuel-II in his efforts to unify the Italian States. Garibaldi led the famous expedition of the thousand to South Italy. In 1867, Garibaldi led an army of volunteers to Rome to fight the last obstacle to the unification of Italy.

questions.text: "Napoleon had destroyed democracy in France, but in the administrative field he had incorporated revolutionary principles." Justify the statement with suitable arguments.
questions.answer:
Following were the reforms brought by Napoleon in the administrative system:
i. The Civil Code of 1804, usually known as the Napoleonic Code, did away with all privilege based on birth.
ii. It established equality before law and secured the right to property.
iii. Napoleon simplified administrative divisions, abolished the feudal system and freed peasants from serfdom and manorial dues.
iv. In the towns too, guild restrictions were removed.
v. Transportation and communication system was improved.

or.text: Identify Napoleon, telling the part played by him in the France.
or.answer:
Napoleon was a great French General, who won many battles for the revolutionary France and raised his nation's prestige. In many parts of Europe, like in the Dutch Republic, Switzerland, Italy and Germany, he simplified administrative divisions, abolished the feudal system and freed peasants from the serfdom and the manorial dues.
There was a time when he had become a terror for all the European monarchs. But in the end, his limited resources collapsed in the face of the fourth coalition of the European nations. He was defeated in the battle of Waterloo in 1815 A.D. and was sent as a prisoner to spend his last days at the small island of St. Helena where he died in 1821 A.D.

questions.text: Why did Mahatma Gandhi relaunch the Civil Disobedience Movement with great apprehension? Explain.
questions.answer:
Gandhiji relaunched the Civil Disobedience Movement with great apprehension because of the following reasons:
i. Mahatma Gandhi had called off the Civil Disobedience Movement as it began to turn violent in many places such as Peshawar and Sholapur. The brutal policy with which the British government responded was equally responsible.
ii. The failure of negotiations at the Round Table Conference in London further added to the bitterness of the situation as Gandhiji came back disappointed.
iii. As Gandhiji returned to India, he discovered a new cycle of repression. The new policies of the British government were a major force that led him to relaunch the movement.
iv. Gandhiji discovered that major leaders such as Jawaharlal Nehru and Ghaffar Khan were put in jail.
v. The government further declared the Congress illegal and imposed restrictions to prevent meetings, demonstrations and boycotts. The national situation eventually forced Gandhiji to launch the movement again but with great apprehension.

or.text: Why did Gandhiji decide to launch a nationwide Satyagraha against the proposed Rowlatt Act of 1919? How was it organized? Explain.
or.answer:
Gandhiji decided to launch a nationwide Satyagraha against the proposed Rowlatt Act of 1919 because:
a. The Rowlatt Act was hurriedly passed through the Imperial Legislative Council.
b. Indian members unitedly opposed it.
c. It gave the government enormous powers to repress political activities.
d. It allowed detention of Indian political prisoners without trials for two years.
e. The Act deprived the Indians of their civil rights.
Satyagraha was organised in the following ways:
a. Mahatma Gandhi wanted non-violent civil disobedience against such unjust laws.
b. It was started with a 'Hartal' on 6th April.
c. Rallies were organized in various cities.
d. Workers in the railway workshop went on strike.
e. Shops were closed down in protest.

questions.text: Most of the objections to the projects arose due to their failure to achieve the purposes for which they were built. Ironically, the dams that were constructed to control the floods have triggered floods due to sedimentation in the reservoir. Moreover, the big dams have mostly been unsuccessful in controlling floods at the time of excessive rainfall. You may have seen or read how the release of water from the dams during heavy rains aggravated the flood situation in Maharashtra and Gujarat in 2006. The floods have not only devastated life and property but also caused extensive soil erosion. Sedimentation also meant that the flood plains were deprived of silt, a natural fertiliser, further adding on to the problem of land degradation. It was also observed that the multi-purpose projects induced earthquakes, caused water-borne diseases and pests and pollution resulting from excessive use of water.

subparts.text: Name the movement against the river project in Gujarat.
Analyse any two merits of multi-purpose river projects.
subparts.answer: Multipurpose projects serve as a source of electricity generation, provide a reliable source of water for irrigation, provide water for domestic and industrial purposes, aid in flood control, facilitate recreational activities, support inland navigation, and promote fish breeding. (any two)

subparts.text: How have the big dams mostly been unsuccessful in controlling floods at the time of excessive rainfall?
subparts.answer: The very dams built to mitigate floods have sometimes triggered floods due to sedimentation in their reservoirs. As rivers carry sediment downstream, it accumulates in the dam reservoirs. Over time, this reduces the storage capacity of the reservoirs. When heavy rainfall occurs, the dams may not have enough space to hold the excess water, leading to uncontrolled releases downstream.

questions.text: What are the reasons for the great change in the caste system.
questions.answer:
There is a great change in the caste system because of various factors such as:
a. The efforts of political leaders and social reformers like Jotiba Phule, Gandhiji, B.R. Ambedkar etc.
b. Socio-economic changes also brought a change in the caste system.
c. Increased urbanization, economic development, better education and job opportunities, occupational mobility has made people less conscious of their caste.
d. There has been a marked attitudinal shift of the people particularly in urban areas who have become more aware.
e. The Constitution of India provided in legal and political principles equality to everybody irrespective of their caste. The prohibition on caste discrimination and untouchability also led to a change in the caste system.

iv. People can put pressure on political parties through petitions, publicity and agitation. Ordinary citizens, pressure groups, movements and media can play a vital role.

questions.text: Democracy is an accountable and legitimate government. Support this statement.
questions.answer:
Democracy indeed exemplifies accountability and legitimacy in governance for the following reasons:
i. Accountability through Elections: In democratic systems, regular elections allow citizens to hold their representatives accountable. Elected officials are aware that their performance directly affects their chances of re-election, motivating them to act in the best interest of their constituents.
ii. Rule of Law: Democracies operate within a framework of the rule of law, in which laws apply equally to all individuals, including those in power. This increases accountability by making government actions transparent and subject to legal scrutiny.
iii. Separation of Powers: Democratic systems often include a separation of powers among different branches of government. This prevents the concentration of power and ensures checks and balances, preventing abuses of authority.
iv. Legitimacy through Consent: Democratic governments derive their authority from the consent of the governed. Through elections, citizens choose their leaders and endorse the legitimacy of the government.
v. Transparency and Public Debate: Democratic governments encourage transparency in decision-making and allow for public debate and discourse. This openness ensures that policies are well-considered and reflect the interests of the people.
(any FOUR can be explained)

or.text: "Democracy is the most popular form of government at present." Justify the statement.
or.answer: Democracy is the most popular form of government today because it ensures equality among citizens, granting everyone equal rights and opportunities regardless of caste, religion, gender or wealth. It enhances individual dignity by respecting freedom of speech, expression, and choice, allowing people to participate in governance and public life. Democratic decision-making is improved through debates and diverse opinions, resulting in fairer and more inclusive policies. Democracy provides peaceful methods to resolve conflicts through dialogue, laws, and elections, preventing violence and promoting stability. It also allows room to correct mistakes, as leaders can be replaced and policies revised through regular elections held at fixed intervals. Laws in a democracy apply to all, including those in power, ensuring justice and fairness. By enabling peaceful changes in leadership and policies, democracy adapts to the evolving needs of society. These features make democracy widely accepted and preferred globally.

A social division based on shared culture. People belonging to the same ethnic group believe in their common descent because of similarities of physical type or of culture or both. They need not always have the same religion or nationality.

subparts.text: How did the Belgian Government solve their ethnic problem? Explain.
subparts.answer:
1. The Constitution says that the number of Dutch and French speaking ministers shall be equal in the Central government. Thus, no single community can make decisions unilaterally.
2. Many powers of the Central Government have been given to the state governments of the two regions of the country. The state governments are not subordinate to the Central government.
3. Brussels has a separate government in which both the communities have equal representation.
4. There is a third kind of government, called the 'community government'. This government is elected by the people belonging to one language community - Dutch, French and German speaking - no matter where they live. (any two)

questions.text: Do you agree that agriculture in India takes place in the unorganised sector?
questions.answer:
Yes, Indian agriculture is mostly concentrated in the unorganised sector. The following factors prove this:
i. Agriculture in India faces the problem of disguised unemployment, i.e. more people are employed than actually needed.
ii. Farmers are employed during harvesting and sowing season while the rest of the time they are unemployed. This underemployment shows that agriculture is unorganised.
iii. Most of the farmers depend on money lenders, rich farmers and relatives for loans instead of banks, and pay high interest.
iv. Farmers do not get any employment benefits such as insurance, medical allowance etc. that the workers in an organised sector are entitled to.

questions.text: How are economic development and human development related to each other?
questions.answer:
Economic development is only one attribute of human development. Though it is a major one, it influences the other attributes also. Human development is a function and barometer of economic development. High GDP growth rates, when distributed equally over a population, will lead to equity. The other human development attributes are:
i. Infant Mortality Rate: the number of deaths per 1,000 live births of children under one year of age.
ii. Literacy rate: the total percentage of the population of an area at a particular time aged 7 years or above who can read and write with understanding.
iii. Net Attendance Ratio: the total number of children in the age group 14-15 years attending school as a percentage of the total number of children in the same age group.
For human development in areas like sanitation and primary education, economic growth is necessary so that people have the funds to pay for these services. Conversely, human development in the form of better nutrition and education is a prerequisite for development. So economic development and human development are two sides of the same coin.

questions.text: Analyse the role of credit in the development of a nation.
questions.answer:
Credit plays a vital role in the development of a nation by facilitating economic growth and improving the standard of living. It increases the production capacity of individual entrepreneurs and companies, allowing them to expand businesses, earn higher profits, and contribute to overall economic prosperity. For industrialists, credit helps manage ongoing production expenses and ensures timely completion of projects, maintaining smooth operations.
Credit also benefits consumers, enabling them to make significant purchases like homes, vehicles, and gadgets, which improves their quality of life and social status. In agriculture, credit allows farmers to buy better seeds, fertilizers, and equipment, resulting in higher crop yields and modernized farming practices. Additionally, access to credit supports research and development, fostering innovation and enhancing the scientific and technological capabilities of the nation. Overall, credit is a crucial instrument for promoting entrepreneurship, productivity, and sustainable development.

or.text: Why is it necessary for banks and co-operatives to extend their lending activities in rural areas? Explain.
or.answer:
Banks and cooperatives should increase lending facilities in rural areas because of the following reasons:
i. The formal sector i.e. the banks and the cooperatives need to engage more in the lending activities because of the disadvantages posed by the informal sector.
ii. The high cost of borrowing discourages many people who wish to start an enterprise. It also significantly reduces the income of the borrower as much of the earnings go into repayment of the loan.
iii. Dependence on informal sources of credit reduces.
iv. To provide more loan facilities to rural households.
v. To save rural people from exploitation. Often it leads to a debt trap where the amount to be repaid is more than the borrower's income and he has to borrow more.
vi. It is important that the formal credit is distributed more equally so that the poor can benefit from the cheaper loans.
vii. The banks and the cooperative societies have to increase the lending facilities to improve the livelihood of the people in rural areas.
